clue.text: Forces them to be kept here in town

definitions.text: Forces them to be kept here in town

parts.words: Forces them to be kept here in town
parts.note: a fortress within a town where armed forces are garrisoned

explanation.surface: A note that troops are to be billeted somewhere in the town.
explanation.definitionFit: A citadel is a fortress guarding a town, where its garrison of troops is kept.

clue.text: Maybe after getting very cold skin like this

definitions.text: Maybe after getting very cold skin like this

parts.words: Maybe after getting very cold skin like this
parts.note: skin cracked and rough from exposure to cold

explanation.surface: Someone's skin has suffered in the frost.
explanation.definitionFit: Chapped skin is cracked and sore, often from cold wind or frost.

clue.text: Has one peer at the back of a book!

definitions.text: Has one peer at the back of a book!

parts.words: Has one peer at the back of a book
parts.note: a peer bears a rank name, and a book's name is printed on its spine

explanation.surface: A nobleman glancing at the end of a volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peer' suggests looking, but it is a nobleman, who holds a rank; 'back of a book' is the spine bearing its name.
explanation.definitionFit: A title is both a noble rank held by a peer and the name printed on a book.

clue.text: By the sound of it, the morning air

definitions.text: By the sound of it, the morning air

parts.words: By the sound of it, the morning air
parts.note: a tune for mourning, which sounds like morning

explanation.surface: Fresh dawn air described by how it sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'air' is a tune, not the atmosphere, and 'morning' is heard as mourning: a lament.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a slow, mournful piece of music for a funeral.

clue.text: Oil rig on Loch Cat!

indicators.note: to rig is to fix or tamper with, so the letters of oil are rearranged

parts.note: Ness is the best-known Scottish loch

explanation.surface: An oil platform set up on a Scottish lake, with a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rig' looks like part of 'Oil rig' but is the anagram signal, making LIO; 'on' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A lioness is a female lion, one of the big cats.

clue.text: Like an animal stable I rebuilt

indicators.note: something rebuilt is put together again in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone says a stable they rebuilt is fit only for beasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuilt' rearranges STABLE and I into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bestial is the adjective for anything resembling or befitting a beast.

clue.text: Has the job of stopping a barrel: went in front and messed the task up

parts.words: Has the job of stopping a barrel
parts.note: a bung is the stopper that closes a cask
led means went ahead of others

explanation.surface: A cooper corked a cask, took charge, and botched the work.
explanation.definitionFit: To bungle is to carry out a task clumsily, making a mess of it.

clue.text: Man wanting principle 0 show Sun colder all over!

indicators.note: scattered all over the place, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man lacking morals shows the sun cooling everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over' rearranges SUN COLDER; '0 show' (likely 'to show' misprinted) only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoundrel is an unprincipled, dishonest man, a rogue.

clue.text: Seems like it's not the original

definitions.text: Seems like it's not the original

parts.words: Seems like it's not the original
parts.note: a copy that resembles something genuine

explanation.surface: Something looks like a copy.
explanation.definitionFit: An imitation is a copy made to resemble a genuine article.

clue.text: As soldiers, they had their good points!

definitions.text: As soldiers, they had their good points!

parts.words: As soldiers, they had their good points
parts.note: cavalrymen armed with sharp-tipped spears

explanation.surface: Faint praise for some old soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good points' sounds like virtues, but it is the sharp tips of their lances.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancers were cavalry soldiers armed with long spears.

clue.text: Called for the time when the sun goes down!

definitions.text: Called for the time when the sun goes down!

parts.words: Called for the time when the sun goes down
parts.note: the part of the day named for the sun having passed its highest point and begun to sink

explanation.surface: A name chosen for the hour of sunset.
explanation.definitionFit: The part of the day after midday, when the sun is descending, takes its name from following noon.

clue.text: Result: tears the outer skin of

definitions.text: Result: tears the outer skin of

parts.words: Result: tears the outer skin of
parts.note: peeling this bulb vegetable makes the eyes water

explanation.surface: A grim result: something rips away an outer skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tears' looks like ripping, but it means weeping: peeling the outer skin of this vegetable brings tears.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting or peeling this pungent kitchen bulb releases vapour that makes cooks weep.

clue.text: Be the first to have a following

definitions.text: Be the first to have a following

parts.words: Be the first to have a following
parts.note: to go in front, so that others come after you

explanation.surface: Advice to be a pioneer and gather disciples.
explanation.definitionFit: To go before something in order or time is to lead, with the rest coming after.

clue.text: Couple to get hitched, making one!

definitions.text: Couple to get hitched, making one!

parts.words: Couple to get hitched, making one
parts.note: a coupling device that joins two things into one, like a pair marrying

explanation.surface: A pair about to marry and become one.
explanation.definitionFit: A linkage is a connecting mechanism, a coupling that hitches parts together.

clue.text: Got rid of the press!

parts.note: a crowd, or press of people, that has been scattered

explanation.surface: Someone has shaken off the journalists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the press' suggests reporters, but it is a pressing crowd that has been broken up and sent away.
explanation.definitionFit: A crowd that is dispersed has been scattered and sent off in different directions.

clue.text: Should get it after being late for "The Good Life"

definitions.text: Should get it after being late for "The Good Life"

parts.words: Should get it after being late for "The Good Life"
parts.note: a reward of heaven after death for those who lived virtuously

explanation.surface: Someone tardy for a TV sitcom should be let in anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' means dead, not tardy, and 'The Good Life' (a British TV sitcom) is a virtuous life.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvation is deliverance of the soul, granted after death to the righteous.

clue.text: Do better than others after a period of abstinence. Very good indeed!

indicators.note: places the abstinence word at the end, following the first piece

parts.note: to excel is to outdo others
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: Advice on outshining others once a fast is over, with praise.
explanation.definitionFit: Excellent means outstandingly good, of the highest quality.

clue.text: We may find neglected buildings in them

definitions.text: We may find neglected buildings in them

parts.words: We may find neglected buildings in them
parts.note: a decayed, broken-down state that abandoned structures fall into

explanation.surface: A remark about where derelict property turns up.
explanation.definitionFit: Neglected buildings collapse into a decayed, wrecked state, being described as in that condition.

clue.text: Pass on to 99,stomach trouble

parts.note: a col is a pass between mountains
IC is 99 in Roman numerals, one less than C (100)

explanation.surface: A message passed on to a number, about an upset stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Colic is severe abdominal pain, especially in babies or horses.

clue.text: Standards of service?

parts.note: regimental flags carried by the armed services

explanation.surface: A question about the quality of service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standards' looks like levels of quality, but it means flags of the armed services.
explanation.definitionFit: A regiment's colours are its flags or standards.

clue.text: Show this out of respect, as it were!

definitions.text: Show this out of respect, as it were!

parts.words: Show this out of respect, as it were
parts.note: rudeness, which comes from being lacking in respect

explanation.surface: An instruction to display something as a mark of respect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of respect' seems to mean as a courtesy; read it instead as having run out of respect.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolence is rude, disrespectful behaviour, the very opposite of deference.

clue.text: Takes an objective view, might one say?

definitions.text: Takes an objective view, might one say?

parts.words: Takes an objective view, might one say
parts.note: has an objective in view, that is, a purpose in mind

explanation.surface: Someone is described as impartial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'objective' seems to mean impartial, but read it as a goal: one with an aim in view.
explanation.definitionFit: To intend is to have something as one's aim or purpose.

clue.text: Badly worried!

parts.note: worried in the sense a dog worries sheep, attacked fiercely

explanation.surface: Someone is very anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' looks like anxious, but a dog that worries sheep attacks and mauls them.
explanation.definitionFit: Savaged means attacked ferociously, mauled as by a wild animal.

clue.text: Not an alloy heated by electricity

definitions.meaning: a pure chemical substance rather than a metal mixture
the coil in a kettle or heater warmed by current

explanation.surface: Something pure in metal that warms up when powered.
explanation.definitionFit: An element is a pure chemical substance, and also an electric heating coil.

clue.text: Perhaps used 'for advertising a sheet

parts.note: a single printed page handed out to promote something

explanation.surface: A sheet of paper that might be put to promotional use.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaflet is a printed sheet distributed to advertise or inform.

clue.text: Fluid — it's vital to us he drinks it!

definitions.text: Fluid — it's vital to us he drinks it!

parts.words: Fluid — it's vital to us he drinks it
parts.note: blood, the fluid we cannot live without, is what this creature drinks

explanation.surface: A warning about a liquid essential to life being drunk by someone.
explanation.definitionFit: In folklore this undead creature feeds by drinking human blood.

clue.text: Times change, little ones!

indicators.note: to change the word times is to alter the order of its letters

explanation.surface: A remark that times are changing, addressed to children.
explanation.definitionFit: Mites are tiny creatures, and the word also means small children.

clue.text: Angry, that is, about a rodent

indicators.note: one piece going round another, so the first word is wrapped around

parts.note: a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: Someone furious, specifically about a rat.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate is a synonym for angry, meaning furious.

clue.text: Join any number from 1-9 to a quarter

parts.note: a single digit is a unit
E, east, is one quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: An instruction to attach a single digit to a fraction.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite is to bring together or combine into one, a synonym of join.

clue.text: The fear of being unconscious

parts.note: the terror experienced while asleep, in a bad dream

explanation.surface: A phobia about passing out.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads as fear of losing consciousness; it is fear felt while sleeping.
explanation.definitionFit: A frightening dream is a terror that comes while the sleeper is unaware.

clue.text: Houses upper echelons of government

parts.note: upper legislative chambers, such as those in many parliaments

explanation.surface: A statement that the top tier of rulers live somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Houses' seems to be a verb, but it is the plural noun for legislative chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: Senates are the upper chambers of legislatures in many countries.

clue.text: Don't agree with what it means

definitions.text: Don't agree with what it means

parts.words: Don't agree with what it means
parts.note: to disagree, to object to the stated sense

explanation.surface: Objecting to the meaning of something.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissent is to hold or express a contrary opinion, to disagree.
